summary: 72-foot steel lookout built on Warm Spring Mountain in Shoshone National Forest in 1927; gone, with no removal date recorded.

facts.design: 72-foot steel X-brace tower with a 7x7 observation cabin
facts.status_note: No tower remains at the site; the register gives no removal date
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Shoshone National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1927 for the tower and cabin; the 1928 newspaper report describes the tower as new construction on the forest that year
Memos show the lookout leaving in September 1958 and plans to man the lookout approved
Added to the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on May 2, 2022

evidence.supports: 72-foot steel tower with 7x7 observation cabin, built 1927
evidence.quote: The 72 foot tall steel, X-Brace tower and 7x7 observation cabin were built in 1927.

evidence.supports: administered by the Shoshone National Forest Forest Service unit

evidence.quote: A new 72-foot steel tower, with glassed in observatory was built on Warm Spring mountain, 10 miles west of Dubois, and connected with the Sheridan Creek Telephone lone by a new line five miles long.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on distance from Dubois: 10 miles west (1928 newspaper quoted on westlookouts) vs 7 miles WNW (firelookout.com). Record coordinates left as they are. Elevation differs slightly: 9,530 ft (register) vs 9518 ft (firelookout.com). Removal date and any later fate are unknown. A YouTube page seen only in search results says the tower was built in the 1930s and burned in 1987; that conflicts with 1927 and with the register's unknown removal date, could not be verified on a readable page, and is not used. A County10 Dubois history article returned HTTP 403 on fetch and is not used. No access status found, so access is omitted. Staffing evidence is the 1958 memos only. The Dubois museum Facebook photo was not fetched and no photo license was checked.
